newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India expected to buy 500,000-600,000/T Mar diesel.
newsitem.headline: India expected to buy 500,000-600,000/T Mar diesel.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is expected to take between 500,000 and 600,000 tonnes of high speed diesel in its tender for March deliveries, traders said on Friday.
This was lower than initial expectations of 600,000-900,000 tonnes and would remove earlier optimism that India's purchases might help to boost sagging prices.
IOC bought 810,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel and 45,000 tonnes of the 0.25-percent grade in two tenders for February deliveries.

One trader said the lower diesel imports expected this time could be because March is the end of IOC's fiscal year and "they might want to limit their cash exposure," and rollover their additional requirements into April.
Traders said low offers were made by a U.S. major for 1.0-percent sulphur diesel at 70 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes cost-and-freight (c&f) Madras or Haldia on the east coast.

State-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp offered free-on-board (fob) cargoes of 1.0-percent material at 47 cents per barrel above MidEast spot quotes, while a European major offered to the east coast at $2.77 per barrel premium to MidEast spot quotes, c&f.
A Swiss trader offered 1.0-percent diesel to the east coast at a $2.90-premium to Mideast quotes and to the west coast at a $2.05-premium, both c&f basis.

Another European major offered 1.0-percent diesel to Goa/Kandla on the west coast at $2.25-$2.45 above MidEast quotes, to Kandla at $1.85-to-$2.00-premium and to the east coast at $3.00-to-$3.25-premium, c&f.
The tender, which closed on January 23, sought 1.0 and 0.25 percent sulphur diesel. It is expected to be awarded later on Friday.
